## Re-measurement (2026-08-11): NOT stale — the signature still fires, and the 7fa8 bounds do not cover the failing path

Triage suspected this bug was killed by commit `7fa8102477` ("Bound malformed overlap judge calls",
2026-08-08 23:25 -0700), on the theory that `request_timeout_limit_s=60` makes a 312-381s band
unreachable. **Measurement refutes that.**

### Method

Scanned every `op=overlap-judge` record across all 17 `/Users/joeoakhart/*/.rebar/usage.jsonl`
logs (1638 records total, 2026-08-06T20:35Z -> 2026-08-12T01:22Z), split at 2026-08-09 (the first
full day after `7fa8102477`).

### Result: the failure mode survives the fix

| window | overlap-judge calls | failed | failed with `duration_s`>120 & `requests`=3 | in the reported 312-381s band |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| pre 2026-08-09 | 754 | 100 | 100 | 9 |
| **post 2026-08-09** | 884 | 329 | **35** | **3** |

Post-fix long failures are not a tail from before the fix — the **most recent eight** are from
yesterday, in this checkout (`/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.rebar/usage.jsonl`):

    2026-08-10T16:31:23Z  dur=308.0s  requests=3  finish_reason=length  output_tokens=48000
    2026-08-10T16:38:24Z  dur=311.2s  requests=3  finish_reason=length  output_tokens=48000
    2026-08-10T16:43:33Z  dur=309.3s  requests=3  finish_reason=length  output_tokens=48000
    2026-08-10T16:50:42Z  dur=316.5s  requests=3  finish_reason=length  output_tokens=48000
    2026-08-10T17:11:59Z  dur=312.5s  requests=3  finish_reason=length  output_tokens=48000
    2026-08-10T17:29:03Z  dur=310.0s  requests=3  finish_reason=length  output_tokens=48000
    2026-08-10T17:34:21Z  dur=310.8s  requests=3  finish_reason=length  output_tokens=48000
    2026-08-10T17:39:48Z  dur=312.2s  requests=3  finish_reason=length  output_tokens=48000

`model=bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`, `provider=bedrock` — so this is NOT the 2876
direct-Anthropic misroute, and not the 895c pre-response 400 (`requests=0`). Same duration band,
same `requests=3`, as originally reported.

### The measured mechanism: `finish_reason=length`, and TWO populations coexist

Every long failure carries `finish_reason=length` and `output_tokens=48000` = **3 requests x a
16000-token output ceiling**. Successful calls in the same log show per-request output of
16091 / 16036 / 16323 / 16102 / 32035 tokens, confirming a 16k-per-request ceiling on that path.
So the answer to AC #2 (retry exhaustion vs output-validation vs provider timeout) is:
**output-validation / retry exhaustion — the model runs to the output ceiling, the structured
parse fails, it retries, three times, ~310s total. It is not a provider-side timeout.**

The decisive observation is that on 2026-08-10 the same checkout logged **both** populations:

* **63 failures with `output_tokens=1024`** — the `7fa8102477` bounds working exactly as designed
  (`output_token_limit=1024`, `structured_retry_limit=0`, `transport_attempt_limit=1`), hitting the
  ceiling once and abstaining cheaply.
* **8 failures with `output_tokens=48000`, `requests=3`, ~310s** — an **unbounded** path, running
  concurrently, in the same directory, on the same day.

### Why the bounds miss it

`7fa8102477` added the four bound parameters to **exactly one** of the two `RunRequest` sites in
`src/rebar/llm/overlap/judge.py` — `judge_batch` (the request at judge.py:171-185). The other
site, `judge_one` (judge.py:133-141), was left with no `output_token_limit`, no
`structured_retry_limit`, no `transport_attempt_limit` and no `request_timeout_limit_s`:

    req = RunRequest(
        system_prompt=system_prompt,
        instructions=instructions,
        config=cfg,
        reviewers=["overlap-judge"],
        mode="structured",
        output_schema="overlap_verdict",
        execution_mode="single_turn",
    )

`judge_one` has no remaining in-tree caller (only `judge_batch` is invoked, at judge.py:284-285,
since c403 batching), so on **current** `main` source the 48k path should be unreachable — yet it
is being logged. The most consistent explanation for two populations in one directory is a
long-lived process serving pre-fix code: this host's `rebar-mcp` MCP server is documented as not
hot-reloading across the hourly `origin/main` auto-update, so an MCP server started before
2026-08-08 23:25 keeps executing the unbounded request while fresh CLI invocations in the same
cwd execute the bounded one. That provenance is inference; the telemetry above is measurement.

### Effect on the verdict (AC #3)

Unchanged and still worth stating explicitly: both `judge_one` and `judge_batch` swallow any
exception and return `_ABSTAIN`, so an overlap-judge failure never fails a review — it silently
disables cross-reviewer dedup for the affected pairs, and duplicate findings survive into the
verdict with no signal that dedup did not run. On the batch path the whole batch abstains at once.

### Status

**Left open.** Remaining work: bound `judge_one` the same way `judge_batch` was bounded (or delete
it as dead code, which also closes the hole), confirm the stale-process hypothesis for the
deployed path, and land the regression test AC #4 asks for. ACs #1-#3 are now answered by
measurement; the fix itself has not been made.

Evidence gathered read-only, no repository or store state changed.
